as_told.title: Biondi SAR scans show hollow tubular structures under Khafre pyramid

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2022 a small team led by an Italian radar specialist, Filippo Biondi, and his engineering colleague, Corrado Malanga, claimed that radar images taken from above, a method called SAR (synthetic aperture radar), showed eight hollow cylinder-shaped structures deep beneath the pyramids at Giza in Egypt. In a later episode Michels describes them as tubes about 20 meters wide under the Khafre pyramid, one of the great Giza pyramids. He calls it one of the boldest claims in archaeology in a century, since if true it would make the question of how and why the pyramids were built far stranger.
